arxiv-1905-01846.title: Equation of states and charmonium suppression in Heavy ion collisions
arxiv-1905-01846.creator: Indrani Nilima a, Vineet Kumar Agotiya a
arxiv-1905-01846.description: Abstract The present article is the follow-up of our work Bottomonium suppression in quasi-particle model, where we have extended the study for charmonium states using quasi-particle model in terms of quasi-gluons and quasi quarks/antiquarks as a equation of state. By employing medium modification to a heavy quark potential thermodynamic observables viz. pressure, energy density, speed of sound etc.

arxiv-2107-03119.title: Variable selection in convex quantile regression: ℒ 1 \mathcal{L}_{1} -norm or ℒ 0 \mathcal{L}_{0} -norm regularization?
arxiv-2107-03119.creator: Sheng Dai
arxiv-2107-03119.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sheng Dai. The curse of dimensionality is a recognized challenge in nonparametric estimation. This paper develops a new ℒ 0 \mathcal{L}_{0} -norm regularization approach to the convex quantile and expectile regressions for subset variable selection. We show how to use mixed integer programming to solve the proposed ℒ 0 \mathcal{L}_{0} -norm regularization approach in practice and build a link to the commonly used ℒ 1 \mathcal{L}_{1} -norm regularization approach.

arxiv-2111-07491.creator: P. S. Chaubal, C. L. Reichardt, N. Gupta, B. Ansarinejad, K. Aylor, L. Balkenhol, E. J. Baxter, F. Bianchini, B. A. Benson, L. E. Bleem, S. Bocquet, J. E. Carlstrom, C. L. arxiv-2111-07491.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by P. S. Chaubal, C. L. Reichardt, N. Gupta, B. Ansarinejad, K. Aylor, L. Balkenhol, E. J. Baxter, F. Bianchini, B. A. Benson, L. E. Bleem, S. Bocquet, J. E. Carlstrom, C. L. Chang, T. M. Crawford, A. T. Crites, T. de Haan, M. A. Dobbs, W. B. Everett, B. Floyd, E. M. George, N. W. Halverson, W. L. Holz. We show the improvement to cosmological constraints from galaxy cluster surveys with the addition of CMB-cluster lensing data.

arxiv-2202-10276.title: Poisoning Attacks and Defenses on Artificial Intelligence: A Survey
arxiv-2202-10276.creator: Miguel A. Ramirez 1 † \dagger, Song-Kyoo Kim 1,2 † \dagger, Hussam Al Hamadi 1, Ernesto Damiani 1, Young-Ji Byon 3, Tae-Yeon Kim 3, Chung-Suk Cho 3, Chan Yeob Yeun 1
arxiv-2202-10276.description: Abstract Machine learning models have been widely adopted in several fields. However, most recent studies have shown several vulnerabilities from attacks with a potential to jeopardize the integrity of the model, presenting a new window of research opportunity in terms of cyber-security.

arxiv-2212-08906.title: Full-Duplex Magnetic Induction Communication: Opportunities and Challenges
arxiv-2212-08906.creator: Muhammad Muzzammil, Saif Al-Kuwari, Niaz Ahmed, Marwa Qaraqe
arxiv-2212-08906.description: Abstract The demand for high data rates is rapidly increasing as the interest in Magnetic Induction (MI) communication-based underwater applications grow. However, the data rate in MI is limited by the use of low operational frequency in generating a quasi-static magnetic field.

arxiv-2405-17412.title: Towards One Model for Classical Dimensionality Reduction: A Probabilistic Perspective on UMAP and t-SNE
arxiv-2405-17412.creator: Aditya Ravuri, Neil D. Lawrence
arxiv-2405-17412.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Aditya Ravuri, Neil D. Lawrence. This paper shows that dimensionality reduction methods such as UMAP and t-SNE, can be approximately recast as MAP inference methods corresponding to a model introduced in Ravuri et al. (2023) , that describes the graph Laplacian (an estimate of the data precision matrix) using a Wishart distribution, with a mean given by a non-linear covariance function evaluated on the latents.

arxiv-2406-13305.title: Multimodal MRI Accurately Identifies Amyloid Status in Unbalanced Cohorts in Alzheimer’s Disease Continuum
arxiv-2406-13305.creator: Giorgio Dolci, Charles A. Ellis, Federica Cruciani, Lorenza Brusini, Anees Abrol, Ilaria Boscolo Galazzo, Gloria Menegaz, Vince D. Calhounfor the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative *
arxiv-2406-13305.description: Abstract Amyloid- β \beta (A β \beta ) plaques in conjunction with hyperphosphorylated tau proteins in the form of neurofibrillary tangles are the two neuropathological hallmarks of Alzheimer’s disease. It is well-known that the identification of individuals with A β \beta positivity could enable early diagnosis.

arxiv-2406-14223.title: Chromatic number of randomly augmented graphs
arxiv-2406-14223.creator: Jan Geest, Anand Srivastav
arxiv-2406-14223.description: Abstract An extension of the Erdős-Renyi random graph model 𝒢 n , p \mathcal{G}_{n,p} is the model of perturbed graphs introduced by Bohman, Frieze and Martin (Bohman, Frieze, Martin 2003). This is a special case of the model of randomly augmented graphs studied in this paper.

arxiv-2407-06463.title: Noise-tolerant public-key quantum money from a classical oracle
arxiv-2407-06463.creator: Peter Yuen
arxiv-2407-06463.description: Abstract Quantum money is the task of verifying the validity of banknotes while ensuring that they cannot be counterfeited. Public-key quantum money allows anyone to perform verification, while the private-key setting restricts the ability to verify to banks, as in Wiesner’s original scheme.

arxiv-2408-02495.title: Preservation of Topological Properties by Strongly Proper Forcings
arxiv-2408-02495.creator: Thomas Gilton, Jared Holshouser
arxiv-2408-02495.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thomas Gilton, Jared Holshouser. In this paper we show that forcings which are strongly proper for stationarily many countable elementary submodels preserve each of the following properties of topological spaces: countably tight; Lindelöf; Rothberger; Menger; and a strategic version of Rothberger. This extends results from Dow’s papers [ 5 ] and [ 6 ] , as well as results of Iwasa ( [ 14 ] ) and Kada ( [ 16 ] ). 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary: 03E05, 54D20, 91A44

1.

arxiv-2502-02287.title: Adaptive Resource Allocation Optimization Using Large Language Models in Dynamic Wireless Environments
arxiv-2502-02287.creator: Hyeonho Noh, Byonghyo Shim, Hyun Jong Yang
arxiv-2502-02287.description: Abstract Deep learning (DL) has made notable progress in addressing complex radio access network control challenges that conventional analytic methods have struggled to solve. However, DL has shown limitations in solving constrained NP-hard problems often encountered in network optimization, such as those involving quality of service (QoS) or discrete variables like user indices.

arxiv-2503-19336.title: Circular Photon Drag Effect in Dirac electrons by Quantum Geometry
arxiv-2503-19336.creator: Guanxiong Qu
arxiv-2503-19336.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Guanxiong Qu. Quantum geometry is a well-established framework for understanding transport and optical responses in quantum materials. In this work, I study the photon drag effect in Dirac electrons using the quantum geometric interpretation of non-vertical optical transitions. Due to the particle-hole symmetry inherent in Dirac electrons, the shift photon-drag photocurrent is dominated by dissipationless Fermi surface contributions, connected to the dipole of quantum metric tensor.

arxiv-2503-20794.title: Can Zero-Shot Commercial API’s Deliver Regulatory-Grade Clinical Text De-Identification?
arxiv-2503-20794.creator: Veysel Kocaman, Muhammed Santas, Yigit Gul, Mehmet Butgul, David Talby
arxiv-2503-20794.description: Abstract We evaluate the performance of four leading solutions for de-identification of unstructured medical text - Azure Health Data Services, AWS Comprehend Medical, OpenAI GPT-4o, and John Snow Labs - on a ground truth dataset of 48 clinical documents annotated by medical experts.

europmc-pmc6704256.title: Sustained microglial depletion with CSF1R inhibitor impairs parenchymal plaque development in an Alzheimer's disease model.
europmc-pmc6704256.creator: Spangenberg E, Severson PL, Hohsfield LA, Crapser J, Zhang J, Burton EA, Zhang Y, Spevak W, Lin J, Phan NY, Habets G, Rymar A, Tsang G, Walters J, Nespi M, Singh P, Broome S, Ibrahim P, Zhang C, Bollag G, West BL, Green KN.

pmc-10563170.title: Differentiating benign and malignant thyroid nodules: A cross‐sectional study on the comparison of diagnostic value of ultrasound elastography and fine needle aspiration biopsy
pmc-10563170.creator: Farnood Rajabzadeh, Ehsan Hassannejad, Iman Akhlaghipour, Mohammad Javad Imen, Atefeh Babazadeh Baghan, Ladan Goshayeshi, Seyed Morteza Taghavi, Shohreh Vojouhi, Asma Payandeh, AmirAli Moodi Ghalibaf
pmc-10563170.description: Background and AimThis study examines the comparison of ultrasound elastography and fine needle aspiration (FNA) in diagnosing thyroid cancers and investigates the use of elastography as the initial diagnostic test of thyroid cancers to avoid the need for invasive diagnostic tests.

pmc-10596390.title: Food emulsifiers and risk of type 2 diabetes: results from the prospective NutriNet-Santé cohort
pmc-10596390.creator: C Salame, B Srour, E Viennois, I Huybrechts, S Hercberg, M Deschasaux-Tanguy, E Cosson, S Tatulashvili, B Chassaing, M Touvier
pmc-10596390.description: BackgroundEmulsifiers are the most ubiquitous food additives. Experimental studies showed an emulsifier-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis stimulating inflammation. This study is the first to investigate the association between food additive emulsifiers and type 2 diabetes risk in a large population-based cohort.

pmc-12639570.title: Evaluating Research Productivity Trends Among Orthopaedic Adult Reconstruction Fellowship Applicants: A Bibliometric Study
pmc-12639570.creator: Emily Tufford, Andrew H. Kim, Peter F. Monahan, Peter Tortora, Luke B. Elias, Andrew B. Harris, Gregory J. Kirchner, Mark W. Mason
pmc-12639570.description: BackgroundThe research benchmarks necessary for a successful adult reconstruction fellowship match remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize and identify trends in the academic profiles of adult reconstruction fellows in the United States.MethodsThe American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons fellowship directory was used to identify U.S. adult reconstruction fellowships programs that listed fellows graduating from 2019 to 2023.

pmc-12644699.title: Hydrodynamic spin-pairing and active polymerization of oppositely spinning rotors
pmc-12644699.creator: Mattan Gelvan, Artyom Chirko, Jonathan Kirpitch, Yahav Lavie, Noa Israel, Naomi Oppenheimer
pmc-12644699.description: Rotors are common in nature — from rotating membrane-proteins to superfluid-vortices. Yet, little is known about the collective dynamics of heterogeneous populations of rotors. Here, we show experimentally, numerically, and analytically that at small but finite inertia, a mixed population of oppositely spinning rotors spontaneously self-assembles into active chains, which we term gyromers.

pmc-12751193.title: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons and coculture conditions regulate the adipogenic differentiation and functionality of human adipose stromal/stem cells
pmc-12751193.creator: Sini Saarimaa, Miia Juntunen, Lotta Isosaari, Reija Autio, Marika Kuuskeri, Susanna Narkilahti, Susanna Miettinen
pmc-12751193.description: BackgroundThe obesity epidemic and associated diseases have increased the need to study human adipose tissue biology and, furthermore, the development of in vitro models of adipose tissues. Human adipose tissue innervation is a relatively understudied research area, and most studies have been performed in animal models.

pmc-13347757.title: Multifocal and Multicentric Breast Cancer: Evaluation of Clinicopathological Features and Survival Outcomes
pmc-13347757.creator: Busra Burcu, Isik Cetinoglu, Aziz Sener, Zeynep Gul Demircioglu, Zerin Sengul, Esma Cerekci, Ramazan Ucak, Cemal Kaya
pmc-13347757.description: ObjectivesThe reported incidence of multifocal breast cancer (MFBC) and multicentric breast cancer (MCBC) varies widely in the literature. This study aimed to compare the clinicopathological characteristics, treatment approaches, and survival outcomes between patients with MFBC/MCBC and those with unifocal breast cancer (UFBC).

pmc-13380536.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Nutritional Management of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Scoping Review
pmc-13380536.creator: Xia Qian, Jie Yu, Qun Zhang, Guanzhen Jia, Junjun Guo, Tianmei Lin
pmc-13380536.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDiet is closely associated with the onset, progression, and prognosis of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). In the absence of specific dietary and nutritional guidelines, nutritional management for IBD patients is fraught with challenges and uncertainties. Existing research indicates that artificial intelligence (AI) has great potential for application in the nutritional management of patients with chronic diseases; however, current research on its use in IBD patients is limited.MethodsThis scoping review was reported in strict accordance with the PRISMA-ScR checklist.
